body.body:
## What

Add `onepipeline readjust <RUN> [--json]` and readjust stacks before review, rework, restacking, dispatch and continuation. Detect host merges, restack and retarget remaining drafts, recover drafts closed by deleted parent branches, and keep recorded bases and Stack blocks current while preserving draft state and description text outside the Stack block.

Batch standings and review feedback, defer republication checks to later triggers, repair failed checks, and surface out-of-order merges and outstanding verdicts without polling or unnecessary store writes. Prevent rework from republishing a draft merged during its dispatch. Refresh the CLI screenshots and demo, and update rustls to 0.23.46 to address RUSTSEC-2026-0346 through RUSTSEC-2026-0349.

## Why

Teams merge approved drafts while the rest of a stack remains in review. Keeping each remaining draft against its surviving parents or the root preserves its own diff and intended merge destination, while batched reads and deferred checks keep GitHub usage low and idle runs silent.

## Additional info

`ReviewReceipt::Performed` gains an `outstanding` field, requiring SDK consumers that construct or exhaustively destructure it to update. The interface additions are recorded in contract-divergence entries 124–126.

body.body:
## What

Supervise manager-started `publish-branch`, `repo-recover` and the new `integrate` command before drafting or landing begins. Preserve ownership through nested flows, refuse acknowledgements that would hide live work, and report failures and process death with closure still owed.

Relay onevcs operation events into flow and originating-run journals. Default readers surface milestones and blockers; detailed flow readers expose every event with resumable cursors. Registration-lock journeys now detect contention through an explicit waiting notice instead of Linux-only process inspection.

## Why

Managers must be able to rely on their watch and Stop hook when a long landing blocks or dies. Durable ownership prevents live work from disappearing behind an acknowledgement, so scarce attention can safely move between sessions.

## Additional info

Adopts published onevcs 0.51.2. Breaking Rust API changes include `Command::Integrate`, `WatchUntil::LandingProgress`, flow-capable monitor arguments, the expanded `watch_conditions()` return array and the producer matcher type update. Existing CLI invocations, stored records and legacy flow cursors remain compatible.

Standalone flows gain no observer; their owners read landing events through flow watch, next and monitor. Associated runs receive mirrored events without reviving settled runs.

## What

Raise the onevcs minimum to 0.50.1 and lock a single resolution carrying the root-workspace member fix. Adapt maintenance reporting to the dependency’s new outcomes, recording and displaying unreadable maintenance configuration.

## Why

Manager publication and worker closeout use the engine’s compiled version-control library. Linking the correction lets valid workspaces whose root is itself a member publish through that path.

## Additional info

onevcs-testing moves to 0.18.2 because it requires exactly onevcs 0.50.1; the previous versions require older onevcs releases. No unrelated dependencies move.

body.body:
## What

`results` reports each skipped node as never attempted and names the
dependencies that skipped it with their own statuses, and the run summary
carries `N never attempted` beside the done count.

`onepipeline attest RUN REFERENCE` now takes a node that settled `failed` as
well as a ready human action: the node stops gating, everything it had skipped
becomes ready inside the loop already running, and `results` shows it as
`settled failed, attested as landed` so a failure is never read as a success.
Any other settlement is refused naming both accepted references. This widens a
published contract and is recorded as open divergence 36, gated by an end-to-end
journey that drives the settlements out of the record itself.

`runs` and `status` print `OBSERVER DEAD` or `NO OBSERVER` beside the driver
word for an executing run, decided from the launch record's graph run, its
ending, and its owner lock rather than the process table; the detached driver
now reaps its observer so that lock can clear. The unread-surface line names the
kinds waiting beside the count and staleness, blocking first, then rarest, with
any remainder counted rather than cut.

Also fixes an end-to-end test that read the driver's log without waiting for it,
racing the driver's own poll and failing two of three macOS runs.

## Why

These are facts a run held but could not state. A skip is re-derived from its
dependency on every pass and the cause was discarded, so `11/27 done` said
nothing about which nodes were never tried or what stopped them — now the node
and the dependency are both named. Nor was there any answer to type when the
failed work had in fact landed: a node here stayed skipped for three days over a
change already merged, so attesting a failure as landed is what releases its
skips. A run whose observer has died is executing unwatched, which is as
operational a fact as a dead driver and was reported nowhere but a log nobody
opens. And a blocking question produces no other signal, so against thousands of
routine updates a bare count buried it — the line now names the kinds waiting.
